name: Net Promoter Score and Root-Cause Decomposition
phase: Metrics, Telemetry, and Innovation Accounting Tactics
hypothesis: We believe that users advocate organically for our product. We will verify this by running an in-app Net Promoter survey with open-ended follow-up prompts, and consider it validated if the overall score meets or exceeds +40, with ≥ 50% of Promoters pointing to the same core capability as their primary reason for recommending it.
schematic: Read at step 3 of the 3-step strip

plan.label: Preparation
plan.text: Add the 0-10 rating prompt after a user completes a core milestone, not at random.

plan.label: Execution
plan.text: Sort answers into promoters, passives and detractors, then ask each for the reason behind the score.

planFull.label: Preparation
planFull.text: Add a standard 0–10 NPS rating prompt to the product interface, triggered only after a user successfully completes a core milestone.

planFull.label: Execution
planFull.text: Group responses into Promoters (9–10), Passives (7–8), and Detractors (0–6). For all scores, trigger an immediate open-ended follow-up asking for the specific reason behind the rating.

planFull.label: Data collection
planFull.text: Calculate the overall score: NPS = % Promoters − % Detractors

warning.label: Passive Satisfaction Inflation
warning.text: High passives (7-8) look healthy but those users switch for price or features.

warningFull: Teams often treat high proportions of Passive respondents (ratings of 7 or 8) as evidence of product health, ignoring that these users regularly switch when a competitor offers lower pricing or better features.
